label: fiction
title: The Locked Floor
setting: A present-day independent radio station where a genuine external threat is followed by a dispute about why one broadcast floor remained locked and who controlled it.
elements: The accused intentionally detained or helped to detain an adult against that person’s will.
The accused intended to compel another person or an institution to act as a condition of the hostage’s release.
The accused knew that the detention and demand were unlawful.
hook: The judge enters as two recordings wait to be played. In one, Leda says she is staying upstairs. In the other, producer Niko Brann demands an investigation be withdrawn while the floor remains locked. Charged with hostage-taking, he denies that he controlled her release or made her the price of his demand.

accused.human: Niko Brann, 36, produces local radio documentaries and was the designated controller for the broadcast floor on the evening in question.
accused.if_guilty: If convicted, sentencing would be decided separately by the judge. The jury's task is limited to deciding whether the prosecution proved the charge.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: The first lock was lawful. What happened later was not, the prosecution says. Niko Brann was the floor controller, stood beside the panel, and was told the central warning had cleared. While Leda remained behind the door, he told the director that the finance report had to be withdrawn before anyone came down. You will be asked to infer control and purpose from that sequence.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: The two recordings do not say what the prosecution says they do. Leda first chose to stay. Niko later made an ugly employment demand, but never made her release its price. A shared safety credential does not identify who set the local hold, and delayed panel notices leave the timing uncertain. Anger during an emergency is not proof that Niko knowingly controlled a hostage.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: Listen to Niko's words in their setting. Arin told him the warning was clear and asked for the floor's release. Niko answered that the report must be retracted before anyone came down. Leda then remained behind a locked door while the designated controller stood near the panel. The shared credential prevents certainty from a single log, but the prosecution says the witnesses, recording, and timing prove one deliberate course.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: Suspicion is not the statutory test. The first recording preserves Leda's voluntary choice. Her later account never places Niko's employment demand in the room. The second recording contains an argument, not a condition of release. The access record identifies the shared RF-2 credential; it cannot say when Niko saw the all-clear or who imposed the local hold, which only the central desk could release. The prosecution has not excluded a safety failure plus an angry, separate grievance.

epilogue: The station separated emergency access controls from employment authority and gave every occupied floor an independent release channel. It also replaced shared credentials with named approvals and synchronised its recording clocks. Leda moved into public-interest finance work after taking extended leave. Niko's documentaries remained in the station archive while the employment dispute followed a separate process. Staff created a trauma-leave fund, and investigators treated the original external threat as an unrelated fictional matter.

beats.reveal_note: Niko's role, access, notice, and words support the prosecution's strongest inference. His qualified admissions stop short of proving who imposed the hold or whether his demand controlled release.

beats.speaker: judge
beats.text: Section 8 of the fictional Hostage-Taking Act excludes anger or a safety mistake. The prosecution must prove Niko intentionally detained or helped detain Leda against her will, used her release as leverage to compel the station, and knew the detention and demand were unlawful. Injury is not required. If, after considering all the evidence, you aren't sure every element was proved beyond reasonable doubt, your verdict must be Not Guilty.
beats.reveal_note: The fictional statute requires proof of detention, conditional leverage, and knowledge as distinct elements. Suspicious speech cannot substitute for control or purpose.

twist: The reference resolution is Not Guilty because neither recording states that Leda's release depended on withdrawal, and the authenticated access record cannot identify who imposed the local hold with the shared RF-2 credential, when Niko saw the all-clear, or whether he could release it. The strongest opposing interpretation remains serious: Niko was the floor controller, stood by the panel, learned during the call that central had cleared the warning, and demanded retraction before anyone came down. Those facts support suspicion, but they do not exclude a safety-control failure plus a separate angry grievance beyond reasonable doubt.

jurors.label: Kian
jurors.persona: Keeps the room focused on which person controlled the detention rather than treating every bad remark as the act itself.

agree: Yes, the first lock was lawful. The disputed act has to come later.
pushback: Vale, where is the evidence that Niko could release that hold?
concede: His 'before anyone comes down' phrase is troubling. I don't dismiss it.
burden_drift: Leda was plainly distressed, and that makes every uncertainty feel like guilt.
burden_correct: We need proof of control and conditional purpose. Niko doesn't have to disprove either.
final: I can't identify who held the floor or find the charged condition. I'm at Not Guilty.

jurors.label: Vale
jurors.persona: Begins from Niko's recorded words, then tests whether the director's interpretation is the only one the words permit.

agree: He put the report first and people coming down second. That's real evidence.
pushback: But did he answer Arin's question about Leda? No—he dodged it.
concede: All right, Kian. The call sounds conditional, but it never actually states the condition charged.
burden_drift: I keep wanting Niko to explain why he chose those exact words.
burden_correct: An explanation would help, but the prosecution still has to prove what he intended.
final: I started at Guilty. The missing answer and shared hold have left me unsure.

jurors.label: June
jurors.persona: Refuses to turn a shared system event into a personal act unless the attribution survives cross-examination.

agree: RF-2 is a credential, not a person. The log can't choose between its two users.
pushback: No, Piri—standing by a panel isn't the same as entering a code.
concede: I accept Niko had access. That makes the prosecution's inference possible.
burden_drift: Because he was floor controller, I catch myself treating the whole system as his.
burden_correct: The charge needs intentional help with detention, not merely a job title.
final: Possible control isn't control beyond reasonable doubt. I remain Not Guilty.

jurors.label: Piri
jurors.persona: Feels Leda's fear strongly, but can separate what Leda experienced from what she learned only after the event.

agree: Leda asked to leave and the door stayed shut. I can't lose sight of that.
pushback: June, she saw Niko at the panel. Doesn't that count for something?
concede: Wait—Leda didn't hear the finance demand. Arin told her about it the next day.
burden_drift: Her fear makes me want to join every later fact into one story.
burden_correct: Fear proves her experience was real. It doesn't identify the person controlling the hold.
final: I believe Leda completely. I'm less sure that her evidence proves Niko used her as leverage.

jurors.label: Etta
jurors.persona: Changes position when the room distinguishes a reprehensible workplace threat from the exact conditional leverage in the statute.

agree: The call gives Niko a motive to use the lock. It doesn't prove that he did.
pushback: Can someone point to the actual condition? I hear an implication, not an answer.
concede: The shared credential changes this for me. I had treated RF-2 as Niko's signature.
burden_drift: His grievance is so personal that I start assuming the hold must be personal too.
burden_correct: The statute asks whether release was the leverage, not whether the argument was unacceptable.
final: I've moved to Not Guilty. The central statutory link is still an inference among alternatives.

jurors.label: Sol
jurors.persona: Gives emergency uncertainty genuine weight without accepting it as a blanket excuse for what followed.

agree: The system may have cleared at 4:18. That doesn't tell us when the panel told Niko.
pushback: Arin told him during the call. The safety explanation gets weaker after that.
concede: I accept the call put Niko on notice somewhere in that four-minute window.
burden_drift: Once Arin says 'all-clear,' I want Niko to justify every second afterward.
burden_correct: A late warning can prove knowledge, but it still doesn't prove who set or controlled the hold.
final: The timing is messy in a legally important way. I can't make it exact by guessing.

jurors.label: Dana
jurors.persona: Initially trusts the apparent precision of the access record, then attends to what its attribution field actually means.

agree: A local hold after an all-clear is powerful evidence that someone made a choice.
pushback: I called RF-2 Niko's code at first. It wasn't; two people could use it.
concede: Toma's answer is precise: the audit identifies the credential, not the operator.
burden_drift: A timestamp looks exact, so I forget the display and call clocks weren't exact.
burden_correct: A reliable log can still be reliable evidence of less than the prosecution needs.
final: The access record no longer gets me to Niko personally. That changes my verdict.

jurors.label: Rhea
jurors.persona: Separates moral judgment about Niko's demand from the prosecution's burden on each statutory element.

agree: The charged leverage is Leda's release. That's the proposition we have to find.
pushback: I think Niko's demand was disgraceful. That isn't a substitute for an element.
concede: The phrase 'before anyone comes down' does connect the grievance to timing. I accept that.
burden_drift: Because the demand was wrong, I start treating every doubtful fact as part of it.
burden_correct: We aren't deciding the employment dispute. We need detention, release leverage, and knowledge.
final: I can condemn the demand and still find the hostage-taking charge unproved.

jurors.label: Tomi
jurors.persona: Trusts authenticated recordings while remaining alert to the difference between a clear voice and an ambiguous proposition.

agree: Both files are authentic. That means we should hear their actual words, not summaries.
pushback: Sorry—where does Niko say Leda's release depends on withdrawal? He never finishes that thought.
concede: I had trusted the displayed call time. Toma's clock correction makes the sequence less exact.
burden_drift: A clean recording sounds definitive even when the sentence itself is ambiguous.
burden_correct: Authentication proves the file wasn't changed. It doesn't prove one interpretation of the words.
final: The recordings are reliable. The prosecution's completed sentence is not recorded in either one.

jurors.label: Fen
jurors.persona: Begins from Leda's fear and Niko's proximity, but listens when another juror distinguishes experience from attribution.

agree: Leda wanted out and Niko was right there. That feels important to me.
pushback: Why tell her to wait for Arin if the finance argument was completely separate?
concede: Piri's right: Leda learned about that argument the next morning, not in the room.
burden_drift: I believe Leda, so I keep wanting every part of her later understanding to be firsthand.
burden_correct: Believing her doesn't mean she could see the code entry or hear the director's call.
final: Her evidence proves fear and a locked door. I'm not sure it proves Niko's statutory purpose.

jurors.label: Aro · foreperson
jurors.persona: Keeps distinct questions distinct and does not force agreement when a juror remains genuinely undecided.

agree: Let's put the prosecution's chain on the table: role, panel, warning, demand, locked door.
pushback: Now the gaps: shared credential, delayed display, no release condition. Which gap can evidence close?
concede: I had treated those five facts as one event. The clocks and witnesses don't make them one.
burden_drift: A locked floor is serious enough that the room may rush past who caused it.
burden_correct: We need all three elements, and each must be beyond reasonable doubt.
final: I see a strong suspicion and a real injury to Leda. I also see unresolved statutory gaps.
